evidence: tests/campaign/native_block_fault.py:369 `return {p.name: sha(p) for p in (store / "transactions").iterdir() if p.is_file()}`; :409 `prior = transaction_files(store)`; :416 `cut = ("frontier-attempted" if scenario == "frontier-dir-eio" else "record-attempted")`; :418 `report["model_program"] = ("fn-bs-frontier-program" ... else "fn-bs-record-program")`. test_native_crash_model.py:43 says `The per-file POST programs (fn-bs-frontier-program, fn-bs-record-program ...) are not reachable on a format-9 store`
fix: Re-target the scenarios to the log route's cuts (log-written / log-fenced via FN_NATIVE_POST_FAULT, or recordbarrier). Expect EIO on the journal segment's fence and on journal/'s directory fsync, and observe the history through native_log_observation.
reviewer: native_block_fault.py:368-369 transaction_files iterates store/transactions, which a log store does not have (io.lisp:4017 'No allocator file and no transactions/'), so :409 raises right after init/post. It also arms FN_NATIVE_POST_FAULT=record-attempted:stop. io.lisp:4836-4877 accepts only the cuts in +fnn-post-model-cuts+ / +fnn-post-log-model-cuts+ (record-attempted is in neither) and only the eio|kill actions, so the selector would fault anyway. The campaign is dead on the shipped format.
scenario: Every scenario (record-dir-eio, frontier-dir-eio, record-dir-sigkill, record-cut-snapshot) raises FileNotFoundError at line 409 right after `store init`, because a log store has no transactions/. FN_NATIVE_POST_FAULT=record-attempted:stop is not in +fnn-post-model-cuts+ either. So the only device-level EIO and SIGKILL evidence for directory barriers cannot run on the shipped format. The only test of the module (test_native_block_fault_ownership.py) checks pid-ownership helpers with mocks, so nothing shows the campaign is dead.
title: Block-fault campaign drives the retired per-file programs and reads store/transactions/
